newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia voucher privatisation delayed until winter.
newsitem.headline: Croatia voucher privatisation delayed until winter.

text.p: Croatia's mass privatisation may be delayed until winter because of logistics hold-ups in the proposed voucher scheme, Assistant Privatisation Minister Damir Ostovic said on Tuesday.
"Some things are running a little late, so we can talk about this coming winter rather than autumn (for the launching)," Ostovic told Reuters.
He said authorities were still working on a register of beneficiaries including war victims, displaced people and other citizens who were left empty-handed in the company buyouts.
Up to 350,000 people were supposed to get vouchers, which would later be swapped for shares in firms from the government portfolio.
A list of between 500 and 600 companies with assets worth nominally around $2.5 million was being drawn up and would be presented later this month, Ostovic said but declined to venture any names.

Parallel with these preparations, the ministry would choose their consultant in an extensive media campaign, aimed at raising the level of public awareness about the scheme among potential beneficiaries.
Ostovic said it had shortlisted nine foreign firms with experience on similar mass privatisation and capital market projects.
They are to submit concrete proposals by September 15.
Some 50 percent of the Croatian economy has been sold off through management and employee buyouts, launched in 1991.
But utilities, temporarily nationalised at the time, have so far been left untouched and it still remains unclear whether at least parts of them might be included in mass privatisation.
Apart from these assets, the government still owns sections of vital tourist, shipping, pharmaceutical and food-processing industry which could draw most interest among bidders.

The rest are leftovers in partly privatised but relatively unattractive firms or shares in strategic ailing sectors, like shipbuilding which still require a sizeable amount of cash to set them on the path to recovery and eventual profitability. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
